programmes.d: Comedian David Steinberg talks about going to Theological school before his career as a comedian. And Kenneth Branagh also joins the fun.
Glenn Close discusses two movies that couldn't be more different--"Fatal Attractions" and "The Big Chill."
Tim Allen, Melanie Griffith and......the great dog photos by famed photographer William Wegman.
Woody Harrelson joins Johnny again, this time talking about....doing Yoga before joining the show.
Actor Craig T. Nelson recalls his first and (disastrous) appearance on The Tonight Show. Also chats about car racing and his teenage son, an aspiring actor who has difficult hair.
Garry Shandling was a regular guest and always had something new and fun to discuss. This time, the topics are laundromats and Disneyland!
Garry is joined by Jimmy Stewart on this episode, who talks about working with Carol Burnett Bette Davis and others.
This time around Garry talks about turning 30, Chinese food and...sex education.
Garry Shandling is ALWAYS funny, whether he's talking about his hair, pets, or traffic tickets.
Only on "The Tonight Show" will you see Patrick Swayze talking about a song he wrote called "Sweet June Farts."
Garry claims that he bombed during his previous appearance so this time he delivers the goods, covering everying from Sonny Bono to Captain & Tenille.

When Johnny Carson encounters the animal kingdom, it's always a great time! Animal expert and advocate Joan Embery brings some fascinating creatures into the studio, educating and entertaining both Johnny and you.
Snakes...why did it have to be snakes? Because animal expert Joan Embery brought them, along with a goose and a marmoset!
Leonard J. Waxdeck joins Johnny to talk about the bird calling contest he sponsors, and treats the audience with a demonstration from some of the winners.
Jim Fowler, zoologist and host of the famed "Wild Kingdom" program, brings a vulture and two oppossums into the studio, along with some tigers that had previously appeared on the show as cubs.
What's Joan Embery brought for Johnny this time? A Gila Monster and an anteater, for starters.
Leonard Waxdeck returns to the panel, with more incredible bird callers in tow.
The famed Zippy The Chimp, along with his close friend Jack Rynsky, takes his turn on the panel with Johnny.
One of late-night TV's great hosts, Tom Snyder confesses it's hard being Johnny's guest. Tom also describes his life in California and bites back at his many critics.
Johnny's heir apparent David Letterman recalls his first appearance on The Tonight Show, his Indiana childhood and his penchant for power tools.
Fellow talk show host Dick Cavett covers a lot of ground: girl pigeons, the guy who invented the bra, legendary fighter Jack Johnson and the Germans' sense of humor.
Dick Cavett in jogging shorts? Johnny describes Cavetti's jitter-calming pre-show run. Cavett tells the story of a guest who died on his show and then...does a magic trick.
Sex expert Dr. Ruth Westheimer talks about her new book, "Dr. Ruth's Guide for the Sexually Perplexed", and shares some of the funniest questions she gets asked.
Fellow talk show host Dick Cavett talks about his early days in the business and what it was like to write jokes for Johnny.
